questions.stem: What is 'eine Abiturientin'?
options: A female student in her first year at university
A female student taking or holding the Abitur
A female teacher who marks Abitur papers
The female principal of a Gymnasium
questions.explanation: 'Der Abiturient' and 'die Abiturientin' are students in their final year sitting the Abitur, or who have just passed it. The plural is 'die Abiturienten'.

questions.stem: What is 'der Abiball'?
options: A formal ball celebrating the end of the Abitur
A football match played between students and their teachers
A party held on the first day of Year 12
A dance class taken before the exams
questions.explanation: The Abiball is a formal evening, usually after the certificates are handed out, where graduates celebrate with their families and teachers. It is similar to an Australian formal.

questions.stem: What is 'der Abistreich'?
options: A strike held by students in protest against the exam timetable
A written exam taken at the end of school
A speech given by the top student
A prank the graduating class plays on their school
questions.explanation: 'Der Streich' means a prank. On the Abistreich day, graduates might take over the school, set games for teachers or decorate the building. 'Der Streik' is a strike.

questions.stem: What is 'das Abimotto'?
options: A punning slogan chosen by the graduating year
The official rules for the Abitur exams
The school motto printed on every final certificate
A farewell song sung by the teachers
questions.explanation: Each year group picks a witty motto, often a pun on 'Abi', and prints it on hoodies, the Abizeitung and banners.

questions.stem: What is 'die Abizeitung'?
options: A newsletter the school sends to parents weekly
A keepsake magazine the graduates make about their year
A local newspaper listing every student's final exam results
The official notice of the exam dates
questions.explanation: The Abizeitung is a keepsake magazine, like a yearbook, with profiles of students and teachers, quotes and memories. Exam results are private and not published.

questions.stem: What happens during 'die Mottowoche'?
options: Students go on a different excursion each day
Teachers swap classes with each other each day
Students dress up to a different theme each day
Students sit an exam in a different subject each day
questions.explanation: In the Mottowoche the graduating class comes to school in costume, with themes such as 'Kindheitshelden' or 'Bad Taste' on each day.

questions.stem: What is 'die Zeugnisübergabe'?
options: The meeting where teachers check the marks
The day students return their textbooks
The parents' evening at which families are told the final grades
The ceremony where final certificates are handed out
questions.explanation: 'Das Zeugnis' is the certificate or report and 'übergeben' means to hand over. The ceremony usually has speeches and music, and is the formal end of school.

questions.stem: What is 'die Abschlussrede'?
options: A summary chapter at the end of a school textbook
A farewell speech at the graduation ceremony
The last question in an oral exam
A teacher's letter of resignation
questions.explanation: 'Der Abschluss' is the completion of school and 'die Rede' is a speech. Like a valedictory speech, it looks back on the school years and ahead to the future.

questions.stem: 'Sie hat das Abitur mit 1,0 bestanden.' What does this mean?
options: She passed with the lowest pass grade
She failed by a single point
She passed in only one of her exam subjects
She passed with the best possible grade
questions.explanation: German grades run from 1 (sehr gut) to 6 (ungenügend), so an Abitur average of 1,0 is the best result. 4,0 is the lowest pass.

questions.stem: In Austria the final exam is 'die Matura'. How does the Maturaball often differ from a German Abiball?
options: It is organised by the government, not students
It takes place in the first year of school
It is often held months before the final exams
It is held only for students who failed
questions.explanation: Austrian graduating classes often hold their Maturaball in autumn or winter of the final year, before the exams. The German Abiball usually follows the results.

questions.stem: 'Nach den Prüfungen fahren viele australische Schulabgänger zur Schoolies Week an die Küste.' What does the sentence say?
options: After their exams many Australian school leavers go to the coast for Schoolies
Before their exams many Australian students study at the coast for a week
After their exams many Australian teachers take school leavers on a trip
Many Australian school leavers spend a week working at the coast after exams
questions.explanation: 'Schulabgänger' are school leavers and 'nach den Prüfungen' means after the exams. They travel to the coast to celebrate, which is what Schoolies Week is.

questions.stem: 'Mir gefällt, dass beim Abiball auch Eltern und Lehrer mitfeiern. Bei unserem Formal in Brisbane waren nur Schüler dabei.' What does the writer like about the Abiball?
options: That the ball is held in Brisbane rather than somewhere in Germany
That teachers organise the ball for their students
That families and teachers celebrate along with the students
That only students are allowed to attend the ball
questions.explanation: 'Mitfeiern' means to join in the celebration. The writer contrasts this with her Brisbane formal, where only students were present.

questions.stem: 'Die Zeugnisübergabe markiert für viele das Ende der Kindheit und den Beginn eines neuen Lebensabschnitts.' What significance is given to the ceremony?
options: It marks the start of the final school year
It marks the move into a new stage of life
It is the most important exam of school life
It is mainly a chance to meet the teachers
questions.explanation: 'Markieren' means to mark, and 'ein neuer Lebensabschnitt' is a new phase of life. The ceremony is presented as a rite of passage out of childhood.

questions.stem: What does 'Der Abiball wird zum Teil von den Eltern finanziert' mean?
options: The Abitur ball is partly paid for by the parents
The parents are partly paid for the Abitur ball
The Abitur ball was paid for by the parents
The parents will pay for part of the Abitur ball
questions.explanation: 'Wird ... finanziert' is the present actional passive, and 'von den Eltern' names who pays. The past would be 'wurde finanziert'.

questions.stem: 'Der Schulleiter sagte in seiner Rede, die Abiturienten könnten stolz auf sich sein.' What did the principal say?
options: That the graduates should have been far prouder of their results
That the graduates could be proud of themselves
That he himself was proud of the graduates
He asked whether the graduates were proud
questions.explanation: 'Könnten' reports his words (Konjunktiv II replacing Konjunktiv I 'können', which looks like the indicative), and 'sich' refers to the graduates themselves.

questions.stem: What does 'Ich wünschte, die Schulzeit wäre noch nicht vorbei' mean?
options: I wanted school to be over already
I hope school will finish soon
I knew school wasn't over yet
I wish my school days weren't over yet
questions.explanation: 'Ich wünschte' plus Konjunktiv II ('wäre') expresses a wish contrary to fact: school is over, and the speaker wishes it weren't.

questions.stem: What does 'Nach dem Abi gönnen sich viele erst einmal eine Auszeit' mean?
options: After the Abitur many begrudge others a break
After the Abitur many first plan a long career break abroad
After the Abitur many first treat themselves to a break
After the Abitur many first refuse to take a break
questions.explanation: 'Sich etwas gönnen' means to treat oneself. 'Eine Auszeit' is time out, and 'erst einmal' means 'first of all'.

questions.stem: Which word completes 'Die Aula ___ gerade für die Zeugnisübergabe geschmückt.' ('is being decorated')?
options: hat
würde
wird
ist
questions.explanation: 'Gerade' shows an action in progress, so the actional passive with 'wird' is needed. 'Ist geschmückt' would describe the finished state.

questions.stem: What does 'das Ehrenamt' mean?
options: A position of honour in the army
Unpaid voluntary work for the community
An honorary degree from a university
A paid post in local government
questions.explanation: An Ehrenamt is an unpaid role done for the good of others, such as coaching a junior team. People who do it are 'Ehrenamtliche'.

questions.stem: What is 'der Bundesfreiwilligendienst' (BFD)?
options: A federal voluntary service open to all ages after school
A compulsory year of community service for all school leavers
A government job scheme for unemployed graduates
A university program training social workers
questions.explanation: The BFD lets people of any age who have finished full-time compulsory schooling volunteer, for example in care, sport or culture. Volunteers receive pocket money, not a wage.

questions.stem: Why was the Bundesfreiwilligendienst introduced in 2011?
options: Voluntary fire brigades were joined into one service
Compulsory military service, and with it civilian service, was suspended
Too many young people were doing a gap year abroad
Universities wanted all new students to gain some practical work experience first
questions.explanation: When conscription was suspended in July 2011, the civilian alternative (Zivildienst) ended too. The BFD was created so that volunteers could fill gaps in social services.

questions.stem: What is 'das Freiwillige Ökologische Jahr' (FÖJ)?
options: A gap year spent travelling between national parks
A paid traineeship at a renewable energy company
A voluntary year working in environment and nature protection
A compulsory year of ecology and biology studies at a university
questions.explanation: Like the FSJ in social work, the FÖJ is a volunteer year for young people, but in environmental work, such as nature reserves or environmental education.

questions.stem: What is 'die Freiwillige Feuerwehr'?
options: A fire brigade staffed by volunteers
A city fire brigade of paid firefighters
A fire safety course taught in schools
A company that sells fire extinguishers
questions.explanation: Most German towns and villages rely on volunteer fire brigades, much like rural fire services in Australia. Large cities also have professional brigades.

questions.stem: What is 'das Technische Hilfswerk' (THW)?
options: A technical college that trains apprentices
A government office that tests the safety of cars and trucks on the road
A charity that repairs computers for schools
A federal civil protection agency made up mostly of volunteers
questions.explanation: The THW helps in floods, storms and other disasters, and almost all its members are volunteers. Testing cars is the job of organisations such as the TÜV.

questions.stem: 'Samstags helfe ich bei der Tafel und gebe Lebensmittel aus.' What is 'die Tafel' here?
options: A restaurant that trains young chefs
A charity passing on surplus food to people in need
A school canteen run by parent helpers
A supermarket chain that sells groceries at the full retail price
questions.explanation: The Tafeln collect food that shops would throw away and give it to people on low incomes, relying largely on volunteers. In a classroom, 'die Tafel' is the board.

questions.stem: An Australian volunteer surf lifesaver would find a counterpart in which German organisation?
options: die Bundeswehr
der TÜV
die DLRG
der ADAC
questions.explanation: The DLRG (Deutsche Lebens-Rettungs-Gesellschaft) trains volunteer lifeguards for beaches, lakes and pools. The ADAC is a motoring club.

questions.stem: Which word completes 'Seit zwei Jahren engagiere ___ mich in der Flüchtlingshilfe.'?
options: sich
ich
mich
mir
questions.explanation: The time phrase is in first position, so the verb comes second and the subject 'ich' follows it; the reflexive 'mich' already appears. 'Sich engagieren' means to be actively involved.

questions.stem: 'Durch mein Ehrenamt im Sportverein habe ich gelernt, Verantwortung zu übernehmen. Außerdem macht es sich gut im Lebenslauf.' Which benefits are mentioned?
options: Better fitness and travel abroad
A new language and a coaching licence
Learning responsibility and a stronger CV
New friends and extra pocket money
questions.explanation: 'Verantwortung übernehmen' means taking on responsibility, and 'macht sich gut im Lebenslauf' means it looks good on a CV.

questions.stem: 'Viele Vereine finden kaum noch Freiwillige. Junge Leute wollen sich oft nicht langfristig binden, sondern lieber bei einzelnen Projekten helfen.' What is the challenge?
options: Young people have no interest in volunteering
Clubs refuse to take on young volunteers
Volunteer projects have become far too short to be worth the effort
Young people prefer short projects to long commitments
questions.explanation: 'Sich langfristig binden' means committing for a long time. Young people still help, but 'lieber bei einzelnen Projekten', which makes it hard for clubs to fill regular roles.

questions.stem: 'Ein Freiwilligendienst ist schön und gut, aber wer kann es sich leisten, ein Jahr lang fast ohne Geld zu arbeiten?' What concern is raised?
options: Volunteer services are too short to be worthwhile
Not everyone can afford a year on very little money
Volunteering for a year is a waste of young people's time
Volunteers earn more than people in regular jobs
questions.explanation: 'Sich etwas leisten können' means to be able to afford something. Volunteers receive only pocket money, so the speaker worries that volunteering suits those with family support.

questions.stem: What does 'Wer sich ehrenamtlich engagiert, tut nicht nur anderen etwas Gutes, sondern auch sich selbst' say?
options: Only people who help themselves should volunteer
Volunteers do good for others, not for themselves
Volunteering benefits the volunteer as well as others
Volunteering helps others but harms the volunteer
questions.explanation: 'Nicht nur ... sondern auch' means 'not only ... but also'. The sentence claims volunteers gain something themselves, such as skills, friends or satisfaction.

questions.stem: What does 'Ohne die Freiwilligen gäbe es in vielen Dörfern keine Feuerwehr' mean?
options: Volunteers have replaced fire brigades in villages
Without volunteers many villages would have no fire brigade
Many villages have volunteers but no fire brigade
Villages without a fire brigade are asking for volunteers
questions.explanation: 'Gäbe' is the Konjunktiv II of 'es gibt', describing an unreal situation: the brigades exist only because of volunteers.

questions.stem: 'Laut einer Umfrage seien junge Menschen engagierter als ihr Ruf.' What does the sentence report?
options: Young people say they are less committed than they used to be
A survey says young people's reputation is better than deserved
Young people are asked to be more committed to surveys
A survey says young people are more committed than their reputation
questions.explanation: 'Laut' means 'according to', and 'seien' (Konjunktiv I) reports the survey's finding. 'Ihr Ruf' is their reputation, which the survey says underrates them.

questions.stem: What does 'Wäre ich nicht so knapp bei Kasse, würde ich ein FSJ im Ausland machen' mean?
options: I did a voluntary year abroad in order to save money
Although I was broke, I did a voluntary year abroad
If I weren't short of money, I'd do a voluntary year abroad
Because I'm short of money, I'm doing a voluntary year abroad
questions.explanation: 'Knapp bei Kasse' means short of money. The verb-first clause with 'wäre' is a condition without 'wenn', and 'würde ... machen' gives the unreal result.

questions.stem: 'Mein Bruder hat ein Jahr beim THW mitgemacht. Seitdem weiß er, was er beruflich will: Er möchte Bauingenieur werden.' What effect did volunteering have?
options: It led to a paid job at the THW
It persuaded him to stay in volunteering
It helped him decide on a career
It made him give up his building career
questions.explanation: 'Seitdem' (since then) links the volunteering to his clear career goal of becoming a civil engineer. Nothing suggests he was paid by the THW.
